rationale: The supplied verse 75/38 reproduces the example exactly: ʕAbər yatu mbalašle šoʕəl w mʕaṭəš w mʕaraṭle, with the same translation. Verse 115/311 instead concerns arriving home, a distressed man and a woman offering to sacrifice sons for Gorgis; it contains neither this example nor an occurrence of mbalaš. Remove that reference while retaining the already correct 75/38; no replacement verse is conjectured.

data.turoyo: U ḥolo Daḥḥo omər: "Annaqla itawu, gdəmmina!" Mbalašle bi čirokayḏe, u ḥolo Daḥḥo omər:
data.translation: Onkel Daḥḥo spricht: Jetzt setzt euch hin, daß wir erzählen! Er begann sein Märchen, Onkel Daḥḥo sprach:

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; b-marked tale complement, contrasted with the inherited verbal complement.

data.turoyo: Mbalašle, mbalašle Gorgis kməǧġəl i qəṣṣa, aydarbo hawi, aydarbo ʕabiri li škafte, aydarbo u ǧənni, mən maḥkelelalle, komaḥkele.
data.translation: Da begann Gorgis die Geschichte zu erzählen: wie sie in die Höhle hineingegangen waren, und was der Geistermann ihnen erzählt hatte, das erzählte er ihm.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; k-Infectum complement and immediate restart, quoted once for both tokens.

data.translation: <...> We will begin with the first story; <...>

rationale: Thin II.1 Infectum; first-plural future and b-marked starting text.

data.turoyo: Alyas ʕAntar: Lo, lo, lo. Uʕdo lo. Kubaʕle hawo. Mbalašli b ġer mede.
data.translation: Alyas Antar: No, no, no. Not yet. That needs doing. I have started on something else.

rationale: Thin II.1 Preterit has three after round 1; first-singular plus b ġer mede broadens the activity complement.

summary: II.1 selects b- plus an activity noun (bi čiroke) or a verbal complement (šoʕəl, kməǧġəl). Complement type does not establish a new meaning.
The two 115/300 tokens are an immediate restart/repetition, not separate onset events. Their shared sentence is quoted once.
Existing contact comparisons remain unchanged; these occurrences show selection patterns, not a new etymological result.
No new Idiomatic phrases: beginning a tale is a normal activity complement of anfangen.
Jan's English is project machine translation, copied only as supplied and not used to establish senses. All interpretations were checked against the Turoyo.
The m-less bulašwo token is evidence for register/dialect variation worth checking, not sufficient evidence of a complete new stem-I base pair.
Jan's explicit mb- forms continue ordinary II.1. Round 1's supplementary Ritter citation question is not resolved by these unrelated Jan passages.

Existing blš-2.II.t.preterit.1 cites 115/311; readers report no mbalašle there, while supplied 115/300 clearly has two tokens. Collate 115/311 before replacing its supplementary citation; its verse was not supplied in this job.
At Jan 2.4/654, is bulašwo an independent I begin form, contracted II, or a figurative engage/touch use? Confirm the base pair before adding a stem.
Confirm vocalism of future gədmbalšina; no source normalization has been made.
Beginning with the first story and beginning something else confirm round-1 b-activity complementation; no separate idiom or sense.
